name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs—open and merged—for two weeks. This gives us real data on its impact without risking disruptions. The trade-off is temporary noise in PR reviews, but the insight outweighs the clutter.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode trains reviewers to dismiss *all* autofeedback as noise, not just false positives—risking permanent erosion of trust in automated signals. A better alternative: run PR-Agent in shadow mode only on *merged* PRs for one week, then compare review quality metrics before and after. Settle it by measuring reviewer engagement drop and false-negative rate in the shadow window.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on merged PRs only, but log the autofeedback for *all* PRs—open or merged—so we still capture the full dataset without cluttering active reviews. This cuts the noise for reviewers while preserving the data needed to measure impact.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode only on merged PRs for one week, logging autofeedback for all PRs. This keeps active reviews clean while still capturing the full dataset to measure impact. The trade-off is delayed visibility into open PRs, but we avoid training reviewers to ignore all automated signals—a bigger risk than missing a week of data.
